messages:
maria: incident bot paged us for Dedicated capacity p99 spike in us-west-2 (multiple customers). looks like autoscaler didn't provision fast enough. paging: @oncall 

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #inc-1767123456 — Dedicated pool saturation in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Runbook: dedicated-pool-saturation.

lee: seeing p95 up ~3.2s -> p99 ~12s for streaming responses. queue depth on pool_42 jumped from 40 -> 900 in ~2m.

maria: confirmed. metrics: 
- pool_42 connections: 1200
- queue_depth: 915
- warmup_inflight: 0
- autoscaler_event: attempted scale +4 nodes at 1767123468 but handshake failed (timeout)
- latency p95 3.2s, p99 12.1s, streaming stall count +260

derek: logs show handshake timeouts to the allocator: ``ERROR handshaker: timeout waiting for node ready (deadline 30s)``. looks like NVMe attach delays on the new instances.

sre-liz: customer-impact? which customers on pool_42? jess (cs) can you pull affected accounts?

jess (cs): pulling now — Customers A, B, and one high-traffic PLG tenant showing 40% error-rate increase (mostly stream disconnects). notifying account reps.

eng-runtime: quick note: the runtime will do prefix caching once nodes are warmed; but warmup jobs were queued and never completed because the new pods failed readiness checks. Possibly kernel driver mismatch on the AMI that blocks our GPU init.

lee: timeline: traffic spike started 1767123458 -> autoscaler triggered at 1767123468 -> nodes provisioning 1767123470 -> handshake fails 1767123479 -> queue spikes after 1767123485 and keeps climbing.

maria: mitigation options (trying in parallel):
1) manual scale-up of warm pools in other AZ (us-west-2b) and route new requests (fast but OS/network hop).
2) failover routing to us-west-1 (higher latency but keeps throughput).
3) emergency throttle on non-SLA routes (reduce multi-tenant background jobs).
4) temporary model downgrade to smaller quantized variant for affected customers.

ops-bot: ``/asgs list pool_42`` -> shows 0 healthy extra nodes, 4 pending.

derek: agree with 1 + 4. I'll start manually bringing up prewarmed instances in us-west-2b with alt-AMI (known-good). if that doesn't finish in 4m, we should route to us-west-1.

sre-liz: @eng-runtime can we force warmup tasks to skip large-weight downloads so readiness won't block? maybe start runtime without some optional artifacts.

eng-runtime: we can flip the feature flag warmup_strict=false which accepts reduced artifact sets and marks node ready earlier. doing it now.

maria: flipping warmup_strict -> false on pool_42 controllers (rolling). patch applied at 1767123498.

lee: after flag flip: warmup_inflight jumped to 220 and many nodes reported ready. queue depth started to shrink to 700 within ~30s. p95 down to 2.1s, p99 7.8s. streaming errors reduce but still elevated.

jess (cs): customers A and B reporting intermittent high latency but no new disconnects after 2m. CS has opened proactive email to top-tier tenant.

derek: starting manual deploy of alt-AMI prewarm in us-west-2b. command: ``./infra/provision --pool pool_42 --ami ami-12good --count 6 --prewarm``. ETA ~3m.

maria: also enabling emergency throttles: lowered default concurrency for free-tier in the routing layer to 0.7x at 1767123508. this should free some burst headroom.

eng-runtime: note: model downgrade is impactful to quality. recommend as last resort for mid-tier tenants only. can prepare a fast-quantized model for tenant-B if needed.

ops-bot: new nodes become healthy at 1767123524 (4/6), prewarm tasks started. pool_42 healthy_count: +4.

lee: good, queue depth at 320. p95 1.3s, p99 4.6s. streaming stall rate still ~+40 above baseline. investigating tail RPCs: many stalled at READ from KV cache miss + remote fetch.

eng-runtime: pushing a fix to reduce remote fetch fallbacks for prefix cache (disable some remote cold-paths) to limit extra latency spikes. applying to prod canary on 2 nodes.

sre-liz: can we quantify customer impact so we can include in postmortem? current window 1767123458 -> 1767123530 considered degraded. p99 aggregated across affected routes peaked at 12.1s. approximate GAU (requests impacted) ~18k.

jess (cs): confirmed impacted requests: ~17.9k across 3 customers, top-tier tenant saw 10% increase in timeout errors. we've sent an incident notice to them.

maria: containment summary: 
- warmup_strict=false applied -> nodes marked ready earlier.
- manual alt-AMI prewarm -> +4 healthy nodes restored capacity.
- emergency throttle on non-SLA flows reduced pressure.
- rollback autoscaler handshake to increase timeouts for this cloud image (temp config).

derek: autoscaler handshake timeout increased to 90s as temporary mitigation at 1767123541. also filed infra ticket #INF-4729 to root cause AMI NVMe attach delays.

lee: after actions: p95 0.9s, p99 2.2s, queue depth stable ~35. streaming stall delta back to +3. baseline error rates returning.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated. severity reduced to P2 at 1767123555. next: postmortem and remediation plan.

maria: agreed. action items:
- INF-4729 (derek) investigate AMI/driver mismatch + long-term fix + controlled AMI rollout.
- ENG-RUNTIME to add safe warmup_strict toggle and monitoring (sre-liz + eng-runtime).
- Routing team to implement auto-failover policy to alternate AZs when handshake fails twice in 60s.
- CS to notify affected customers and provide RCA timeline (jess).

jess (cs): will send follow-up email within 2 hours and coordinate CS outreach.

sre-liz: will prepare a short postmortem with timeline, impact numbers, and suggested improvements. draft ETA 24h.

maria: closing handoff. if anything regresses, re-page. thanks everyone for quick coordination. :heart:
